claims: The Artemis II mission successfully concluded on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II mission concluded with a safe splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
The Artemis II splashdown occurred at 8:07 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
8:07 p.m. EDT equals 5:07 p.m. PDT for the Artemis II splashdown.
The Artemis II mission lasted 10 days.
The Artemis II crew consisted of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis II mission was the first crewed flight to the moon since 1972.
The Artemis II crew successfully completed a "bullseye landing".
The Artemis II crew was recovered by NASA.
The Orion capsule underwent a 5,000-degree Fahrenheit re-entry.
The Orion capsule was protected by its heat shield.
The Orion capsule deployed parachutes for a soft landing.
The Artemis II crew is safe and in good health following their return
